description:
## Why (placeholder)

PKCS#11 is the universal API for HSMs, smart cards, and TPM-backed key/cert stores. Enterprise PKI, FIPS-mode deployments, code-signing setups, and PIV/CAC smart card environments all surface trust roots as cert objects on a token. The `pkix-truststore-pkcs11` adapter handles "list cert objects on this token, return Vec<TrustAnchor>".

## Scope

Adapter crate that opens a PKCS#11 session, enumerates `CKO_CERTIFICATE` objects with `CKA_TRUSTED=true` (or filtered by other criteria), extracts `CKA_VALUE` (DER bytes), and feeds them through `pkix_truststore::from_der_iter(...)`.

Token kinds in scope:
- General PKCS#11 tokens (Yubico HSM, Thales, AWS CloudHSM, Azure Dedicated HSM, SafeNet)
- YubiKey PIV
- Smart cards (PIV/CAC, OpenPGP)
- TPM 2.0 via `tpm2-pkcs11`
- SoftHSM (for testing)

## API shape

```rust
// Configuration: which library, which slot, optional filter predicate.
pub struct Pkcs11Config {
    pub library_path: PathBuf,         // path to .so / .dll PKCS#11 module
    pub slot_id: Option<u64>,          // None = first slot with token
    pub pin: Option<String>,           // for tokens that require login to enumerate
    pub trusted_only: bool,            // filter on CKA_TRUSTED=true
}

// Open session, enumerate cert objects, extract DER, build TrustAnchors.
pub fn load(config: &Pkcs11Config) -> Result<Vec<TrustAnchor>, Error>;

// Lower-level: provide an open session, get back anchors. Useful when the
// consumer already has a session for other operations (signing, etc.).
pub fn load_from_session(session: &cryptoki::session::Session) -> Result<Vec<TrustAnchor>, Error>;

pub use pkix_truststore::TrustAnchor;

pub enum Error {
    Pkcs11(cryptoki::error::Error),
    Truststore(pkix_truststore::Error),
    NoTrustedCertificates,
}
```

## Dependencies

- `pkix-truststore` (workspace) — for `from_der_iter` and `TrustAnchor` re-export
- `cryptoki` — Oxidized PKCS#11 bindings (RustCrypto-adjacent, well-maintained)

## Open design questions (decide at implementation time)

- **Which `CKA_TRUSTED` semantic?** PKCS#11 v2.40 added `CKA_TRUSTED` for cert-as-trust-anchor; older tokens lack it. Adapter must work with both — `trusted_only=false` falls back to "all cert objects on the token."
- **Login behavior for tokens that need it.** PIV cards typically require PIN to enumerate. Take `pin: Option<String>` and call `login()` only when present and required.
- **Multi-slot iteration?** Some tokens expose certs across multiple slots. Probably a separate `load_all_slots(config)` helper rather than complicating the main entry point.
- **Should this carry per-anchor `CKA_TRUST_*` attribute info forward?** PKCS#11 has trust attributes for serverAuth, clientAuth, codeSigning, etc. Mapping these into `pkix-path::TrustAnchor` requires the per-anchor-trust-policy extension that is currently out of scope for `pkix-path`. Document this gap; pass through what we can without it.

## Out of scope

- Using HSM-stored private keys for path validation (private key stays on token; we only extract public cert DER).
- PKCS#11 session lifecycle management beyond "open, enumerate, close." Consumers managing long-lived sessions use `load_from_session`.
- Token discovery / hot-plug (`C_WaitForSlotEvent`).

## Status

PLACEHOLDER. No implementation work scheduled.

## Relates to

- PKIX-lhm4 (`pkix-truststore` Tier 1 core).
notes:
Placeholder bead per architectural conversation 2026-05-08. The PKCS#11 adapter pattern is the second-most-common non-file trust source after OS-native; filing alongside pkix-truststore-system gives the project two reference adapter crates that establish the "API call → DER → from_der_iter" canonical pattern.
Marked blocked 2026-05-10: bead is explicitly labelled '(placeholder)' in its title and starts with '## Why (placeholder)'. This is a scope-capture stub, not a unit of immediate work. Unblock when there is a concrete consumer requiring HSM/PKCS#11 trust source integration.
Stub crate created 2026-05-11: pkix-truststore-pkcs11/ exists with empty skeleton at 0.1.0, ready for namespace publication. Substantive content per this bead's description (PKCS#11 session management, CKO_CERTIFICATE enumeration with CKA_TRUSTED filtering, error mapping) remains the open work.

When the PKCS#11 adapter is implemented, the anticipatory pkix-truststore dep and cryptoki deps get added to the stub crate's Cargo.toml at that time.
Escalating to human (do-beads loop, 2026-05-11): bead description explicitly says 'Status: PLACEHOLDER. No implementation work scheduled. File concrete sub-beads when a consumer requests this adapter or when the architectural pattern needs validation against a real platform integration.' Autonomously expanding into concrete PKCS#11 adapter work would violate that explicit gating. Decision needed:

  (a) Keep as tracking-only placeholder and re-label / defer so it stops surfacing as ready every session.
  (b) Expand into concrete sub-beads now for a specific PKCS#11 backend. SoftHSM is the natural Tier-1 target for testability since real HSMs / smart cards require hardware Mark may or may not have access to.
  (c) Close as documented-API-skeleton and reopen if / when a consumer asks.

Recommendation: (a). The cryptoki crate API surface is large, the test surface depends on which hardware can be exercised, and the per-anchor trust attribute mapping (CKA_TRUST_*) requires extending pkix_path::TrustAnchor which is out of scope for pkix-path. A SoftHSM-only Tier-1 happy-path implementation is ~3 days of work but only validates the API shape, not real-token interop, so the cost-vs-value is poor until a consumer surfaces.
Relabeled 2026-05-11 (Mark): human → placeholder. Bead text already explicitly states "Status: PLACEHOLDER. No implementation work scheduled." The human label was causing the bead to surface in the autonomous ready queue every session; the placeholder label expresses the same gating intent without the false signal that a maintainer decision is pending. Unblock by either:
  (a) a consumer asking for HSM/PKCS#11 trust integration, or
  (b) a maintainer choosing to do a SoftHSM-only Tier-1 happy-path implementation (~3 days, validates API shape but not real-token interop).
Deferred to 2027-05-11 (Mark): same rationale as PKIX-8h87 — placeholder label captures nature, defer hides from bd ready without faking a pending decision. Clear the defer if a consumer surfaces.
